A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Compact Metric Space|compact metric space]] and $T: X \to X$ [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Metric Spaces)|continuous]].
Then there exists a [[Definition:Borel Measure|Borel]] [[Definition:Probability Measure|probability measure]] $\mu$ on $X$ such that:
:$T_* \mu = \mu$

B_source.statement:
Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]] [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] [[Definition:Convex Set (Vector Space)|convex]] subset of a [[Definition:Topological Vector Space|topological vector space]].
Let $\FF$ be a commuting family of continuous [[Definition:Affine Transformation|affine]] maps $K \to K$.
Then the maps in $\FF$ have a common [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]].

substitutions.the compact convex set: the Borel probability measures on the space, in the weak-star topology
substitutions.the continuous affine self-map: the pushforward operator induced by the map
substitutions.a fixed point of the map: a measure invariant under the map

derived.the fixed point condition: the pushforward of the measure equals the measure
derived.the affineness of the operator: the pushforward preserves convex combinations of measures

object_map.reformulation: Lift the map to an operator on measures, so invariance becomes a fixed point of that operator.

validity_conditions: The probability measures on a compact metric space form a convex set that is compact in the weak-star topology, by the Banach-Alaoglu theorem together with the Riesz representation theorem.
The pushforward operator is affine, since it preserves convex combinations, and is weak-star continuous because the map is continuous.
A single map is a commuting family of one element, so the theorem applies directly; the general form additionally handles commuting families of maps.
proof_plan:
Let $\map {\mathcal M} X$ be the set of Borel probability measures on $X$ with the [[Definition:Weak-* Topology|weak-$*$ topology]].
By the [[Riesz Representation Theorem]] and the [[Banach-Alaoglu Theorem]], $\map {\mathcal M} X$ is compact, and it is clearly convex.

Define $\map {T_*} \mu = \mu \circ T^{-1}$.
$T_*$ is [[Definition:Affine Transformation|affine]].
For $\phi \in \map C X$, $\displaystyle \int \phi \rd \paren {T_* \mu} = \int \phi \circ T \rd \mu$, so $T_*$ is weak-$*$ continuous.
By the [[Markov-Kakutani Theorem]] applied to $\FF = \set {T_*}$, there exists $\mu$ with $T_* \mu = \mu$.
